questions.question: In digital integrated circuit design and Static Timing Analysis (STA), what does the term 'critical path' refer to?
options: The power delivery line carrying the highest current density across the chip.
The longest combinational path between two synchronous storage elements, which sets the upper bound on the maximum clock frequency.
The clock distribution network branch exhibiting the largest capacitive load.
The shortest delay path between an input and output pin that can cause hold time violations.
The test sequence scan path with the largest total number of scan flip-flops.

questions.question: In a classic in-order pipelined processor, what is the primary purpose of data forwarding (also called operand bypassing)?
options: To resolve Write-After-Write (WAW) hazards by dynamically remapping architectural registers.
To allow out-of-order retirement of instructions while preserving precise exception handling.
To bypass cache misses by fetching instruction operands directly from main memory.
To route an execution result directly to a dependent instruction in an earlier pipeline stage, eliminating stalls caused by Read-After-Write (RAW) hazards.
To pass branch target addresses directly to the fetch unit before instruction decode completes.

questions.question: In the physical design and power integrity analysis of an integrated circuit, what is 'IR drop' and why is it problematic?
options: Unintended high-frequency electromagnetic radiation causing substrate noise in adjacent analog blocks.
A degradation of gate oxide breakdown voltage caused by hot carrier injection over extended operational lifetimes.
A reduction in effective supply voltage along the on-chip power distribution network caused by wire resistance and current draw, leading to increased cell delays and possible timing violations.
Parasitic capacitive coupling between adjacent high-speed signal lines that induces clock skew.
An exponential increase in subthreshold leakage current caused by local temperature hotspots.

questions.question: Why are directory-based cache coherence protocols preferred over snooping-based protocols in systems with large numbers of processor cores?
options: Directory-based protocols avoid broadcasting coherence requests over a shared interconnect by tracking sharing status point-to-point, preventing network bandwidth bottlenecks as core count scales.
Directory-based protocols eliminate the need for coherence state bits (such as valid and dirty bits) inside private L1/L2 caches.
Snooping-based protocols are fundamentally unable to handle non-blocking memory access requests across shared caches.
Directory-based protocols move coherence management entirely into the operating system software, reducing on-chip transistor counts.
Snooping-based protocols can only support write-through caches, whereas directory-based protocols allow write-back caches.

questions.question: In bulk CMOS integrated circuits, what is the underlying physical mechanism of 'latch-up'?
options: Excessive quantum tunneling through thin gate dielectrics that permanently locks the PMOS transistor into a conducting state.
Electrostatic breakdown in shallow trench isolation that creates trapped charges and inverts channel polarity.
Avalanche breakdown occurring at drain-bulk pn junctions when transient supply voltages exceed breakdown thresholds.
Void formation in high-density metal lines due to directional atomic transport under high current gradients.

The triggering of parasitic cross-coupled NPN and PNP bipolar transistors forming a silicon-controlled rectifier (SCR) structure, creating a high-current, low-impedance short circuit between VDD and GND.
